trust_decision.summary: lejp_parse decides whether the nesting depth of untrusted JSON fits the fixed ctx->st[LEJP_MAX_DEPTH] parse stack and ctx->i[LEJP_MAX_INDEX_DEPTH] index stack; at the pinned commit each bound check runs after the write/increment (check-after-write, off-by-one).

landing_point.why: Summary names the LEJP JSON parser and a buffer overflow; the commit title is 'fixes for MAX_DEPTH', which leads straight to the add_stack_level depth check in lejp_parse.

fix_sites.entry_point: lejp_parse() public API: root-level outer array '[' (LEJP_IDLE)
lejp_parse() public API: root '{' with LEJP_FLAG_FEAT_OBJECT_INDEXES
lejp_parse() public API: nested '{' value with LEJP_FLAG_FEAT_OBJECT_INDEXES
lejp_parse() public API: every push (string, key, object, array) via add_stack_level

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All five fix sites are inside lejp_parse() in lib/misc/lejp.c; no site in another module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Nothing to dismiss inside the published scope: all sites are one function and one concept (move bound check before the write). The only nearby same-mechanism code is lecp_parse_subtree (lib/misc/lecp.c:354), which a solver could reasonably dismiss as the CBOR parser, i.e. a different format/advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: JSON nested right up to the limit (sp reaching LEJP_MAX_DEPTH-1, ipos filling all LEJP_MAX_INDEX_DEPTH slots) must still parse, and the LEJP_FLAG_FEAT_LEADING_WC path match after the i[] push must still see the new index; a fix that rejects one level early or reorders the match breaks legitimate deep documents and wildcard index reporting.

O6_input_shapes: nested object '{' as value with LEJP_FLAG_FEAT_OBJECT_INDEXES
any stack push (key string, value string, object, array) at add_stack_level

O8b_injection_room.sibling: lecp_parse_subtree() does &ctx->st[++ctx->sp] with no bound check against LWS_ARRAY_SIZE(ctx->st) (LECP_MAX_DEPTH 12)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Real code already: a second implementation of the same depth-stack push in the CBOR parser; lecp_push (lib/misc/lecp.c:177) has a pre-check but the subtree helper skips it. Callers in lib/cose/cose_validate.c:612,708 invoke it at shallow depth, so an injected deeper caller or a lowered LECP_MAX_DEPTH would make it reachable.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: lejp_check_path_match writes ctx->wild[ctx->wildcount++] with no bound against LEJP_MAX_INDEX_DEPTH
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same index-array family in the same file; currently bounded only by '*' count in developer-supplied path patterns, so a variant matching wildcards against parsed (attacker) path segments would be a believable maintainer addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: lejp_parser_push bounds pst_sp with '+ 1 ==' equality; a planted variant using post-increment check-after-write would mirror the published bug in the nested-parser stack
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: lws_struct (lib/misc/lws-struct-lejp.c:107,132) and jrpc (lib/misc/jrpc/jrpc.c:124) push child parsers driven by input shape; a maintainer could easily have written it with the same check-after-increment idiom.

O9_family: memory safety: out-of-bounds write on fixed-size parser depth/index stacks (off-by-one, check after write)

O10_build.project_tests: minimal-examples-lowlevel/api-tests/api-test-lejp/main.c (ctest api-test-lejp); fix diff adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change only the add_stack_level check at lib/misc/lejp.c:862 to pre-check sp, leaving the four i[ctx->ipos++] write-then-check sites untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/cose/cose_validate.c:637 increments cps->sp into cps->st[3] (lib/cose/private-lib-cose.h:79) without a visible bound; COSE state, not the LEJP sink, not pursued.
lib/misc/lejp.c:532,734,778 decrement ctx->ipos at root with LEJP_FLAG_FEAT_OBJECT_INDEXES without a zero check; possible underflow, not pursued.
unverified: Reachability per config: with default LEJP_MAX_DEPTH=64 / LEJP_MAX_INDEX_DEPTH=64 (include/libwebsockets/lws-lejp.h:188,195), ipos appears to stay <= sp+1, so the i[] overflow looks reachable mainly when INDEX_DEPTH < DEPTH (LWS_ESP_PLATFORM 16/12); not confirmed by running.

At defaults the st[] defect leaves ctx->sp == LEJP_MAX_DEPTH after LEJP_REJECT_STACK_OVERFLOW (lib/misc/lejp.c:862); OOB access then depends on a caller re-entering lejp_parse (lib/misc/lejp.c:252,258,262) or the FAILED callback reading st[sp]; which consumers do so was not traced.
